### Identification

$$
\begin{aligned}
E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i Y_i^{(a_i, \mathbf{a}_{\mathscr{N}_i})}  \right] &= E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[Y_i^{(a_i, \mathbf{a}_{\mathscr{N}_i})}  | \mathbf{L}] \right] \\
\end{aligned}
$$ We can start by using the law of iterated expectations. Then we can evaluate the inner expectation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
 E[Y_i^{(a_i, \mathbf{a}_{\mathscr{N}_i})} | \mathbf{L}]  &=  E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i}, L_i,  a_i,  g_{Y}(\textbf{L}, i),      h_{Y}(\textbf{a}, i)         )   | L_i , g(\mathbf{L}, i)] \phantom{, A_i = a_i, h_Y(\textbf{A}_{\mathscr{N}_i}) = h_Y(\textbf{a}_{\mathscr{N}_i})} \\ 
        &=  E[f_{Y}(...)   | L_i , g(\mathbf{L}, i), A_i = a_i, h_Y(\textbf{A}, i) = h_Y(\textbf{a}, i)] \\
        &=   E[Y_i                                      | L_i , g(\mathbf{L}, i), A_i = a_i, h_Y(\textbf{A}, i) = h_Y(\textbf{a}, i)] \\
\end{aligned}
$$

::: aside
-   In the first line, we use the definition of counterfactual variable $Y_i^{(a_i, \mathbf{a}_{\mathscr{N}_i})}$ given in @eq-homogenous-dag. We also use the loyalty of the exposure mapping for $Y_i^{(a_i, \mathbf{a}_{\mathscr{N}_i})}$ to graph $\mathscr{G}$ to simplify the conditioning statement.

-   In the second line, we use the fact that given fixed $\mathbf{L}$, $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i}, L_i, a_i, g_{Y}(\textbf{L}), h_{Y}(\textbf{a}))$ is a function of random variable $U_{Y_i}$. Since $U_{Y_i}$ is independent of $U_{A_i}$ as well as $U_{A_j}$ for $j \in \mathscr{N}_i$, $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i}, L_i, a_i, g_{Y}(\textbf{L}), h_{Y}(\textbf{a}))$ is independent of $\mathbf{A}$.

-   In the final line, we use the definition of observed variable $Y_i$ given in @eq-homogenous-dag.
:::

We are left with this functional

$$
E[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i  E[Y_i |  L_i , g(\mathbf{L}, i), A_i = a_i, h_Y(\textbf{A}, i) = h_Y(\textbf{a}, i) ]]
$$
